class: Carnival Splendor (Concordia-class hull, marketed as "Splendor-class" since she is the only Carnival-flagged unit)
sisterShips: Costa Concordia (same hull design, lost in the 2012 grounding/capsizing)

zones.what: Deck 6 (Upper) sits directly on top of Deck 5 (Promenade), which holds the Red Carpet Disco/Nightclub, the Royal Flush Casino, Our House Sports Bar, and the atrium stage.
zones.effect: Guests booking Deck 6 have repeatedly asked whether cabins above the casino, the sports bar and the main lounge/atrium are noisy; one cruiser found a casino stage with live music was 'right below' the cabin and another pair specifically worried about cabins 6255/6308 sitting above Our House Sports Bar and the main lounge.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and anyone planning an early night should avoid Deck 6 over the casino/nightclub/atrium footprint; late-night partiers or people who don't mind bass through the floor won't notice.
zones.source: cruisecritic.com member review ('right below our cabin' casino stage) and boards.cruisecritic.com Splendor-specific threads on 6255/6308 and 'cabin above the casino'; cruisemapper.com deck 5 plan listing the Red Carpet Disco, Royal Flush Casino and Our House Bar on that deck.

zones.what: Deck 9 (Lido) carries the Splendido midship pool and an aft pool with bars and a stage, while Deck 8 (Verandah) cabins sit one deck directly beneath that footprint.
zones.effect: Mid/aft Deck 8 cabins are one deck below the pool decking, lounge-chair traffic, and outdoor stage rather than two or three decks removed, so morning chair-dragging and pool-party noise carry more directly than on lower decks.
zones.mattersTo: Sea-day nappers and light sleepers should favor forward Deck 8 or drop to Deck 7/6 mid; pool-deck-adjacent convenience seekers may prefer this trade-off.
zones.source: cruisemapper.com Splendor Deck 9 plan describing the 'Splendido Pool area (midship)' with an outdoor stage and the aft pool, combined with the Deck 8 profile's midship/aft cabin weighting.

zones.what: Deck 6 cabins are the deck cruisers specifically ask about when it comes to lifeboats blocking the straight-down balcony view on Splendor.
zones.effect: A CruiseCritic thread asks directly about Splendor room 6362 and whether the lifeboat will be in the way when looking down; the general pattern on ships this size is that boats block the view straight down while the horizon view stays open.
zones.mattersTo: Photographers who want an unobstructed view of the waterline directly below should avoid Deck 6; anyone who just wants open-air and a sea-level horizon view is unaffected.
zones.source: boards.cruisecritic.com thread 'Does Deck 6 Have an Obstructed View' naming Carnival Splendor room 6362; general obstructed-view mechanics corroborated by cruisecritic.com's obstructed-view explainer.

zones.what: Splendor has 19 interior cabins with real windows that look onto outdoor walkways/observation decks rather than the sea, located forward on Decks 6, 7, 9 and 10 (Carnival's own help desk lists 4J cabins 6201-6206, 7201-7206 and 9201-9203 as having this walkway obstruction).
zones.effect: These 'Interior with Picture Window (Obstructed View)' cabins get natural light but anyone walking the outside promenade can be close to the tinted window; guests are told to keep curtains closed at night for navigation-light reasons.
zones.mattersTo: Budget cruisers wanting a window for light will like these; anyone wanting real privacy or an actual ocean view should skip them.
zones.source: help.goccl.com official Carnival Splendor obstructed-view/porthole page listing exact 4J cabin numbers; corroborated by cruisecritic.com Splendor cabin editorial describing 19 such windows forward on Decks 6, 7, 9 and 10.

zones.what: A small set of forward interior cabins on Decks 1 and 2 (1201, 1202, 1205, 1206, 2211, 2212, 2216, 2217) are Category 1A cabins with two portholes instead of a picture window.
zones.effect: These give a genuinely different (smaller, double-porthole) view rather than a single obstructed window; not a lifeboat or machinery obstruction, just a smaller window format built into the ship at that point.
zones.mattersTo: Cruisers who specifically want a full window should note these are portholes; those who don't care about window size or want the character of a porthole cabin are fine.
zones.source: help.goccl.com official Carnival Splendor obstructed-view/porthole page listing these exact Category 1A cabin numbers.

zones.what: Splendor's Aft-View Extended Balcony (8M on Decks 6-7, 8N on Deck 8) and Premium Vista Balcony (9C) cabins wrap around the ship's aft corners with 50%-larger balconies rather than sitting flush with the straight hull line.
zones.effect: These aft-corner cabins buy a wider, wraparound wake view instead of the standard side-only balcony sightline; Carnival's own marketing highlights the panoramic sky-and-sea vantage this creates.
zones.mattersTo: Wake-view enthusiasts and photographers should target these; budget-focused inside/oceanview bookers won't be affected either way.
zones.source: carnival.com Splendor ship page describing Premium Vista Balcony staterooms as 'designed to wrap around the aft corners'; cruisemapper.com corroborating that these cabins 'are located at the ship's aft corners and offer suite-like amenities, including a wraparound balcony.'

zones.what: Reviewers and cabin guides for Splendor consistently identify forward balconies as windier and midship Decks 6-8 as the calmest, with higher/forward positions feeling the most motion.
zones.effect: A forward-facing balcony gets more wind buffeting and ship movement, especially on Pacific/open-ocean itineraries; a midship cabin on 6, 7 or 8 gives the steadiest ride.
zones.mattersTo: Motion-sensitive cruisers should book midship on 6-8; those chasing dramatic bow views and don't mind wind or movement can take forward higher decks.
zones.source: cruisesnooze.com Splendor review noting forward balconies 'can feel windier' and midship balconies 'offer better stability'; coohom.com Splendor cabin guide identifying Decks 6, 7 and 8 midship as quietest with least motion.

zones.what: Connecting 'family cabins' on Splendor are concentrated on Decks 1, 2, 6, 7, 8 and 11, in categories PT/4E (2-bed), 6A/6B/6C/8B/8C/8D (2-3-4 bed) and 8S (4-bed).
zones.effect: Families/groups wanting an adjoining door have real options across most cabin decks, but anyone sensitive to noise from an adjoining party should ask specifically whether their category is a connecting one before booking.
zones.mattersTo: Families and groups benefit; solo/couple cruisers wanting maximum quiet should ask to avoid connecting-door categories.
zones.source: cruisemapper.com Splendor cabins page: 'Connecting rooms ("family cabins") are located on decks 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, and 11.'

zones.what: Each Splendor cabin deck has small crew/service niches off the main corridor (e.g., an ironing room across from cabin 1425 on Deck 1, an ironing room across from cabin 6391 on Deck 6, and a launderette across from cabin 7339 on Deck 7) rather than a single obvious service block.
zones.effect: Cabins directly across from these niches can see more foot traffic and occasional cart/appliance noise than cabins further down the corridor, even though the space isn't marked as a full galley or crew corridor entrance.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers assigned next to one of these marked niches may want to request a different cabin a few doors down; most guests won't notice.
zones.source: cruisedeckplans.com Splendor deck-by-deck pages flagging the ironing room across from 1425 and 6391, and the launderette across from 7339.

Whether Splendor's hull tapers on the highest cabin decks (10-11) in a way that hides the straight-down view from balconies on those decks — no source addressed this directly.
